test_title: PYST 05: SSC Stenographer 2025: English Language & Comprehension (Held On: 07 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: english
question: Which among the following sentences uses adjective with correct degree of comparison.

options.text: New Delhi is more hotter to Chandigarh.
New Delhi is more hotter than Chandigarh.
New Delhi is hotter to Chandigarh.
New Delhi is hotter than Chandigarh

solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. New Delhi is hotter than Chandigarh .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The question requires identifying the correct use of the 'degree of comparison' in a sentence.
 
• The adjective "hot" is used to compare two places: New Delhi and Chandigarh.
 
• The correct structure for comparing two entities is: **Subject + comparative adjective (-er form or 'more' before the adjective) + than + object.**
 
• In this case, the correct comparison is "hotter than" because "hotter" is the comparative form of "hot."

Correct sentence: *New Delhi is hotter than Chandigarh.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Explanation of incorrect options:**

 
 
• **Option 1:** "New Delhi is more hotter to Chandigarh" is incorrect because "more" and "hotter" cannot be used together. Only one comparative form should be used.
 
• **Option 2:** "New Delhi is more hotter than Chandigarh" is incorrect for the same reason as Option 1—redundant use of "more."
 
• **Option 3:** "New Delhi is hotter to Chandigarh" is incorrect because "to" is not the correct preposition for comparison. The correct preposition is "than."
